  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 96

laridae is the CGAL-backed member of the hypertidy meshing stack. It wraps
CGAL (the Computational Geometry Algorithms Library) — its 2D constrained
Delaunay triangulation and `Delaunay_mesher_2` — behind a *persistent handle*
you can edit and refine incrementally, and it returns the
same vertices / segments / triangles contract as
[cdtr](https://github.com/hypertidy/cdtr) so the backend is a choice, not a
rewrite.

For the bigger picture — where laridae sits among cdtr, RTriangle, GEOS and
earcut, and why the triangles are only part of the story — see
[Triangulation in context](https://mdsumner.github.io/trianglewins/context/).

```{r}
library(laridae)
```

This vignette uses a small base-graphics helper to draw a mesh and, optionally,
shade its triangles by a per-triangle value.

```{r helper}
plot_mesh <- function(tab, by = NULL, main = "") {
  V <- tab$vertices; T <- tab$triangles
  plot(V$x, V$y, type = "n", asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", main = main)
  if (!is.null(by)) {
    pal <- hcl.colors(max(by, na.rm = TRUE) + 1L, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE)
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(T))) {
      ix <- c(T$v0[i], T$v1[i], T$v2[i])
      polygon(V$x[ix], V$y[ix], col = pal[by[i] + 1L], border = "grey80")
    }
  } else {
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(T))) {
      ix <- c(T$v0[i], T$v1[i], T$v2[i], T$v0[i])
      lines(V$x[ix], V$y[ix], col = "grey70")
    }
  }
  points(V$x, V$y, pch = 19, cex = 0.4)
}
```

## The contract tables

A triangulation is described by three tables that every hypertidy mesher
shares. Here is a square with a square hole, as two closed rings of
constraint segments.

```{r square-hole}
x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25)
y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75)
m <- lari_new(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5))

lari_vertices(m)
lari_triangles(m)
lari_segments(m)
```

* **vertices** — `x`, `y`, any attribute columns, the `origin` of each vertex
  (`input`, `crossing`, or `steiner`) and a stable `id`.
* **triangles** — `v0`, `v1`, `v2` (1-based rows of the vertices table),
  `depth` and `depth_distinct` (see below).
* **segments** — the constraint edges `v0`, `v1`, the input `segment` id they
  came from, and `count`, the number of input segments covering the edge.

## Depth: inside, holes, and coverage

`depth` counts the constraint crossings on the way in from outside the convex
hull. For nested rings odd is inside and even is a hole, so the square-with-a-hole
has depth 1 in the ring and depth 2 inside the hole.

```{r depth}
table(lari_depth(m))
```

`depth_distinct` is the same count, but a *doubled boundary* — an edge covered
by several coincident input segments — is crossed once instead of once per
segment. For a simple ring the two agree; they differ when boundaries are
duplicated (a common artefact of per-polygon ring data).

## One-shot triangulation

`lari_triangulate()` builds, optionally refines, and returns the three tables
in one call — the drop-in form that mirrors cdtr's `cdt_triangulate()`.

```{r oneshot}
r <- lari_triangulate(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5),
                      max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25)
plot_mesh(r, by = r$triangles$depth, main = "refined, shaded by depth")
```

## The persistent handle

The handle is what sets laridae apart: points and constraints can be inserted
and removed at any time, vertex ids stay stable, and refinement can continue
or restart after an edit touching only the affected neighbourhood.

```{r handle}
m <- lari_new(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5))
lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25)
lari_counts(m)
```

Edit the mesh and refine again — only the neighbourhood of the edit is redone.

```{r edit}
ids <- lari_add_points(m, c(0.1, 0.15), c(0.1, 0.12))
lari_add_segments(m, ids[1], ids[2])
lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25)
lari_counts(m)$steiner
```

Or advance the mesher one step at a time with the last criteria.

```{r step}
lari_step(m, n = 5)
```

## Refinement: angle, area, and sizing fields

Beyond a global `min_angle` and `max_area`, laridae takes a **sizing field**:
the local maximum triangle area as a function of position (or a grid). Here the
target area grows with `x`, so triangles are fine on the left and coarse on the
right.

```{r sizing}
ms <- lari_new(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1), 1:4, c(2, 3, 4, 1))
lari_refine(ms, size = function(x, y) 0.0005 + 0.01 * x)
plot_mesh(lari_tables(ms), main = "sizing field: fine on the left")
```

## Attributes ride along

Per-vertex attributes passed as `PA` are carried onto crossings and Steiner
points by linear interpolation, so a field defined on the inputs stays
consistent through refinement.

```{r attr}
z <- 2 * x + 3 * y + 1   # a linear field on the inputs
ra <- lari_triangulate(x, y, 1:8, c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5),
                       PA = cbind(z = z), max_area = 0.01)
## a linear field is reproduced exactly at every vertex
max(abs(ra$vertices$z - (2 * ra$vertices$x + 3 * ra$vertices$y + 1)))
```

## Where to next

* `?lari_refine` for the full refinement arguments, including `seeds`, the
  `erase` region, and the edge-length floor.
* [cdtr](https://github.com/hypertidy/cdtr) for the header-only,
  builds-anywhere backend with the same contract.
* [Triangulation in context](https://mdsumner.github.io/trianglewins/context/)
  for how these pieces fit together.
